patients.summary: Healthy graduate student who joined in 2023. In 2025 she had gonococcal PID with pharyngeal infection, then Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis a month later, and in early 2026 a disseminated gonococcal infection treated in hospital; all resolved, retest negative in June 2026.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o woman new to us. Previously followed at a pediatric and adolescent office until she aged out; records requested. Just started a graduate program this month and wanted an adult doctor close to campus.

No ongoing health problems. No meds, no supplements. NKDA. No surgeries. Periods regular, monthly. Sexually active, condoms most of the time, no prior STI that she knows of. No pregnancies.

Family: mother with hypothyroidism found at 45; father with high blood pressure since his 50s. No autoimmune disease or unusual infections in the family.

Social: grad student, lives in an apartment with a roommate. Never smoked, no vaping. A drink or two on a weekend. No drug use.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals as charted. HEENT clear, neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. Mood bright.

Assessment/plan:
- Adult preventive care. Pap today (first one, age 21). Urine GC/CT NAAT; HIV and hep C screens once.
- Discussed condoms with every partner and contraception choices; she will think it over and is not starting anything today.
- Flu vaccine given, L deltoid. She'll get the fall COVID booster at her pharmacy.
- PHQ-2 zero.
- Return in about a year, sooner by text or call.

documents.title: Results Message
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Juniper, your screening tests are all negative: gonorrhea, chlamydia, HIV and hepatitis C. The Pap goes to cytology and usually takes about a week; I'll send that one along too.

documents.title: Prior Pediatric Practice Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 38 pages from the prior pediatric/adolescent office. Contents: well-child and adolescent visits through 2021, growth charts, immunization record. No chronic diagnoses, no hospitalizations, no surgeries. Immunizations entered: MMR and varicella x2, Tdap 2013, MenACWY 2013 and 2018, HPV 9-valent two-dose series 2013-2014. Indexed to chart.

documents.body: Your Pap came back normal. Next one in three years, so fall of 2026. Your old records also came in, and your vaccines are all up to date, including HPV.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Second year of her program, placement went fine. Feels well. Sleeping okay most weeks, busy but not overwhelmed. Still on no meds. Sexually active; condoms usually, she says. No new symptoms, no pelvic pain or discharge. Cycles regular.

PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: comfortable, vitals as recorded. Ears and throat clear. No adenopathy. Heart: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear bilaterally. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. Affect normal.

Plan:
- Yearly GC/CT urine screen sent.
- Flu shot today.
- Pap not due until 2026.
- COVID booster at the pharmacy when convenient.
- Next physical in a year.

orders.reason: fever with pelvic pain and discharge

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called back after her text. Three days of fevers and shaking chills, aching low in the pelvis, a new discharge, and pain with sex. Last period about two weeks ago. No vomiting, eating and drinking.

Needs a pelvic exam and probably same-day treatment. Our office has no speculum slots left today; spoke with the gynecology clinic downtown, who can see her at 9:30 tomorrow. Told her to go to the ED tonight if pain gets much worse, she can't keep fluids down, or she feels faint. She agreed.

conditions.label: Gonococcal pharyngitis and pelvic inflammatory disease
conditions.note: Endocervical and pharyngeal NAAT positive for gonorrhea

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 14 days

documents.title: Gynecology Clinic Letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 08/06/2025
Reason: urgent referral from primary care, fever and pelvic pain

Thank you for sending Ms. Hanlon, 22. For three days she has had fevers with chills, lower abdominal pain, a vaginal discharge, and deep pain with intercourse. LMP two weeks prior. She reports several partners over the past year and says condoms are not used every time. No sore throat.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother hypothyroid (dx mid-40s), father hypertensive (dx about 50); no autoimmune or recurrent-infection history in the family.

Exam: T 101.8 F (38.8 C). Abdomen soft, tender in both lower quadrants without peritoneal signs. Speculum: purulent discharge from the os. Bimanual: cervical motion tenderness, bilateral adnexal tenderness, no mass. Incidentally a single small pustule on the left finger. Oropharynx unremarkable.

Urine hCG negative in clinic. Endocervical and pharyngeal swabs sent for GC/CT NAAT.

Assessment: pelvic inflammatory disease, mild to moderate, suitable for outpatient treatment.
Plan: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in clinic. Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14 days. Avoid intercourse until she and partners are treated; she will notify recent partners. Condoms discussed at length.

Addendum 08/08: NAAT returned. Gonorrhea detected at both the endocervical and pharyngeal sites; chlamydia not detected. Final diagnosis gonococcal PID with gonococcal pharyngitis; treatment above covers both. Patient informed by phone.

Allergies: NKDA.
Gynecology clinic

documents.title: Checking In
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Juniper, I got the gynecology letter and the swab results. How are you feeling? Make sure you finish all 14 days of the doxycycline, take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for a bit after.

documents.title: Re: Checking In
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Much better, thank you. No fever since Friday and the cramping is mostly gone. On day 6 of the pills. I told the people I needed to tell.

reports.text: Technique: transabdominal and transvaginal grayscale and color flow imaging. Uterus anteverted, normal size and contour; endometrium thin and uniform. Both ovaries normal in size with normal follicles and arterial and venous flow present bilaterally. No adnexal mass, no tubo-ovarian abscess, no free fluid. No intrauterine or extrauterine gestation.
reports.conclusion: No ectopic pregnancy. No ovarian torsion. Normal pelvic ultrasound.

reports.text: Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder thin-walled without stones, sludge or pericholecystic fluid; no focal tenderness over the gallbladder with the probe. Common bile duct 3 mm. No intrahepatic ductal dilatation. Right kidney unremarkable. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal right upper quadrant ultrasound. No cholecystitis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED provider note, 09/14/2025

23F, treated about a month ago by gynecology for gonococcal PID with pharyngeal involvement (ceftriaxone, doxycycline). Now with sharp, steady right upper quadrant pain that catches when she breathes in, a week of low fevers, and a dull cramping ache in the lower abdomen. LMP three weeks ago, normal. Reports multiple partners, condoms not consistent.

Meds: none currently. Allergies: NKDA.

VS: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 110, BP 125/75.
Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. RUQ tender, no rebound, no guarding. Lungs clear. Pelvic: cervical motion tenderness.

Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250. AST 70, ALT 85, T bili 1.2, alk phos 120. Urine hCG negative.
Imaging: TVUS without ectopic or torsion; RUQ US normal, gallbladder unremarkable.

MDM: perihepatitis in a patient with recent gonococcal PID; Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome. Cholecystitis and ectopic excluded by imaging. Tolerating PO, pain controlled.

Tx: ceftriaxone 1 g IV given. Discharged on doxycycline 100 mg BID and metronidazole 500 mg BID, 14 days each. Abstain until course done. See PCP within a few days; return for worsening pain, vomiting, high fever.

Allergies: NKDA.
Regional ED

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED Sunday with right upper belly pain that hurt on inspiration; diagnosed with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis after last month's gonococcal PID. Got IV ceftriaxone there; now on doxycycline plus metronidazole, day 3 of 14. No missed doses, tolerating both. Fever broke Monday. RUQ ache is maybe half of what it was; breathing deep is less sore.

Exam: afebrile, HR down to normal range. Mildly tender RUQ, no guarding. Lower abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, improving on treatment. Finish both antibiotics. No alcohol while on metronidazole and for 3 days after. Recheck liver enzymes in a few weeks at her physical.
2. Gonococcal PID/pharyngitis, treated in August.
3. High-risk sexual exposure. HIV and RPR today. Long talk about condoms every time; she was receptive.

Call or text if fever returns.

documents.title: Results Message
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: HIV and syphilis tests both negative. Keep going with the antibiotics, and we'll check your liver numbers at your October physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, combined with follow-up of the late-summer infections.

Finished doxycycline and metronidazole late September. Pain completely gone, both pelvic and under the ribs. No discharge, no fevers. Periods normal. Third year of the program, teaching a section this term.

PHQ-9 3. Never smoker; drinking one or two a week again.

Exam: well. Vitals as charted. Throat clear. Heart regular, no murmur; lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no RUQ tenderness, no lower quadrant tenderness. Skin without lesions.

Assessment/plan:
- Gonococcal PID with pharyngeal infection: treated, resolved.
- Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome: resolved clinically; hepatic panel today.
- Sexual health: condoms reviewed again; she knows to come in for testing with any new partner or symptoms.
- Flu vaccine today. COVID at the pharmacy.
- Pap due fall 2026.
- See in a year.

documents.title: Liver Tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your liver tests are back to completely normal. That fits with the inflammation around the liver having healed. Nothing more to do here.

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted at 7:20, called her back. Since the weekend: high fevers, joints that hurt and puff up and seem to move around (wrists, then knees, now ankles), and this morning she can barely walk to the bathroom. Also small red bumps with white tops on her chest and arms.

With her history this needs blood cultures, a joint tap and IV antibiotics today. Told her to go straight to the ED; a friend is driving her. I called ahead to the ED attending.

events.reason: Fever, migratory joint pain, pustular rash

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED provider note, 02/12/2026. PCP called ahead.

23F with gonococcal PID last August and Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis in September, both treated. Several days of high fever; pain and swelling that has moved between the wrists, knees and ankles, now hard to bear weight. New small red pustules over the trunk and arms. Takes no medications. NKDA. Multiple partners, condom use inconsistent.

VS: T 39.2 C (102.5 F), HR 110, BP 120/75.
Skin: scattered pustules on an erythematous base, trunk and extremities. MSK: affected joints tender and swollen; passive range painful. Abdomen soft.

Procedure: knee arthrocentesis, sterile technique, cloudy yellow fluid. Synovial fluid WBC 20,000/uL, 90% neutrophils. Stain without organisms. Culture sent, pending. Blood cultures x2 and genital/pharyngeal/rectal swabs sent before antibiotics.

MDM: fever, migratory polyarthritis and pustular dermatitis in a young woman with prior gonorrhea; disseminated gonococcal infection. Admit to medicine for IV ceftriaxone.

Allergies: NKDA.
Regional ED

medications.sig: 1 g IV every 24 hours for 7 days

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 02/12/2026, discharged 02/19/2026
Diagnosis: disseminated gonococcal infection (arthritis-dermatitis form)

Course: admitted from the ED after knee aspiration showed inflammatory fluid (WBC 20,000, 90% PMNs, no organisms on stain). Started ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h and completed 7 days. Afebrile from hospital day 2. Joint swelling settled over the first several days; walking the halls by day 4. Pustules dried and crusted.

Micro: blood cultures 2/2 no growth. Synovial culture no growth, final. Endocervical NAAT positive for gonorrhea; pharyngeal and rectal NAAT negative. Chlamydia negative. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

Discharge meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Condition: good.
Instructions: no sex until seen by PCP; partners from the past 60 days need testing and treatment (health department notified per routine). Follow up with PCP in about a week; retest for gonorrhea in 3 months.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since Thursday after a week inpatient for disseminated gonorrhea. Read the discharge summary; cultures all negative, cervical NAAT positive, HIV negative. Finished the full 7 days of IV ceftriaxone in the hospital, nothing to take at home.

Today: no fevers. Joints feel close to normal; knees and ankles no longer swollen, wrists fine for typing. Walked in from the lot without trouble. Spots on her arms have faded to small brown marks.

Exam: afebrile. Wrists, knees and ankles without effusion or warmth, full range without pain. A few flat healing macules on the forearms, no pustules.

A/P
1. Disseminated gonococcal infection, treated, clinically resolving.
2. High-risk sexual behavior. Second gonococcal infection in six months. Talked frankly and without judgment about condoms with every partner, fewer partners, and testing with any new partner. She says the hospital stay scared her. Retest for gonorrhea and chlamydia in about 3 months.

Video check-in in a month.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her office on campus. Feels entirely back to herself. No joint pain or swelling, running again a couple of times a week. Skin marks gone. No fevers since discharge. No pelvic symptoms.

Disseminated gonococcal infection resolved. Plan retest swabs in June when she's in for a visit, about 4 months out from treatment. Condoms, she says, every time now.

results.text: Not detected (endocervical swab); Not detected (pharyngeal swab)

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for the post-treatment retest. Feeling well; no pelvic pain, discharge, sore throat, joint symptoms or rash. Using condoms consistently, she reports.

Exam: vitals as noted. Oropharynx clear. Joints without swelling. Skin clear.

Plan: endocervical and pharyngeal swabs for GC/CT NAAT today. Results by portal. Pap is due in the fall along with her physical and flu shot; front desk to send a reminder in August.

documents.title: Results Message

documents.body: Good news, both swabs were negative for gonorrhea and chlamydia. Enjoy the summer.
